scope.description: One fault-free execution on normally bootstrapped in-memory clusters: a 3-node cluster plus one joining voter, a configuration read on every node, an intervening membership change, a change guarded with the index the API returned, and a control change guarded with the genuine configuration entry index. Identical to the verified predecessor except that the leader-side events are admitted on a leader-scoped admission event.
assumptions: MakeCluster(3) plus MakeClusterNoBootstrap(1) merged and fully connected performs real bootstrap, replication and membership changes through the in-memory transport.
AddVoter's returned future index identifies the configuration entry the client just created, so it is the independent reference for what the configuration index should report.
The read is taken against a configuration that has not changed before the read returns, so it is the configuration the caller would want to guard against.
Between the read and the guarded change the harness performs an intervening membership change, so a correctly guarded change must be rejected.
excluded: Internal configuration tracking used by the main loop, which is obtained through a different path.
Network-transport behaviour and any transport-level effects.
Performance, and callers that ignore the returned index.

basis.prefix: Same prefix as the verified predecessor, built with captured test facilities and real producers only: MakeCluster(3) plus a merged single-node cluster, AddVoter whose future index (3 in the local run) is the reference configuration index, one config_guard_start admission per node, one config_read result per node carrying the returned index, the returned membership and the reference index, then a configuration read whose returned index is reused, an intervening AddVoter (entry 4), a guarded DemoteVoter using the returned value, and a control AddVoter guarded with the genuine index 3. The successor additionally emits leader_change_window_start with the leader's node identity and the reference index immediately before the guarded sequence, and admits the two leader-side comparisons on that event. No storage is pre-filled and no production code is modified.
basis.requirement: The configuration index exposed by GetConfiguration identifies the configuration the same call returned, and a membership change guarded with that value is rejected once the configuration has moved on; a change guarded with the genuine configuration entry index is rejected in the same situation.
basis.responsibility: GetConfiguration's construction of the returned configuration future and nextConfiguration's prevIndex guard, i.e. the client-visible optimistic-concurrency contract for membership changes.

comparisons.description: Every node whose returned configuration contains the four servers: the reported index must identify that same configuration, i.e. match the reference configuration entry index.
Impact: a change guarded with the index the API returned must be rejected because the configuration moved on after the read; it is applied instead.
Control: the same situation guarded with the genuine configuration entry index is rejected with the configuration-changed error, so the guard works when a real index is supplied.

prefix.before: Built with captured test facilities and real producers only: MakeCluster(3) bootstraps a three-voter cluster and elects a leader; a second cluster of one node is merged and fully connected, and the leader adds that node with AddVoter, whose future index (3 in the local run) is recorded as the reference configuration index. The harness then emits one config_guard_start admission per node and, for each node, one config_read result carrying the index and membership returned by GetConfiguration plus that reference index. It reads the configuration again, takes an intervening membership change (a further AddVoter, entry 4), then applies a guarded change using the index the API returned, and finally applies a control change guarded with the genuine reference index. No storage is pre-filled and no production code is modified.

The successor additionally emits leader_change_window_start with the leader's node identity and the reference index immediately before the guarded sequence, and admits the two leader-side comparisons on that event. before.description: Every node: the configuration returned by GetConfiguration contains the four servers while its reported index must identify that same configuration, i.e. match the reference index of the configuration entry.
Impact: a change guarded with the index the API returned must be rejected because the configuration moved on after the read; it is applied instead.
Control: the same situation guarded with the genuine configuration entry index is rejected with the configuration-changed error, so the guard itself works when a real index is supplied.

revision_reason: Only admission scoping changed. In the predecessor (receipt 5466e7c2853749f6849e40362a2cdf00) comparisons 0 and 1 were violated as intended, but the control comparison returned unknown because the leader-only control event was correlated against four per-node config_guard_start admissions, three of which can never produce it ('Admitted operation has no complete applicable result observation'). The successor adds one leader_change_window_start event carrying the leader's node identity before the guarded sequence and admits the two leader-side comparisons on it; the per-node comparison 0 keeps its per-node admission. Producers, cluster shape, parameters and result event names are unchanged, so fresh execution is requested only because the comparison basis changed.
